sections.title: Look Up (New Teaching)
paragraphs: God has given the Holy Spirit to every believer to equip us all for ministry. The work of a pastor is important, but there are many other ways that both men and women can serve in God’s kingdom. The Bible calls other church leaders Servants (Ministers). Paul called the men and women who traveled with him for ministry Co-Workers.
Read
Romans 16:1-16, 16:21-23 (Paul’s Co-Workers)
Tell It as a Story
Can someone tell this story in their own words? … In Romans 16, Paul greets many men and women who were his Co-Workers in Christ. We can learn much from their various roles and ministries.
Teach

(Verse 1) Phoebe was a woman recognized as a servant (a deaconess or minister) of a local church. She supported Paul's ministry and likely delivered this letter to the church in Rome. While the work of teaching in the church assembly belongs to the pastor, a church’s “servants” can do many other kinds of ministry. It is a very honorable role. Remember, even Jesus came as a servant, not to be served!

(Verse 3) Prisca and Aquila were a married couple who traveled with Paul as his co-workers in ministry. They hosted a church in their house and often risked their lives. As husband and wife, they shared the gospel, made disciples, planted churches, and even raised up new leaders like Apollos.
(Verse 5) Epaenetus was the first person in Asia to believe in Jesus! Paul honors his courage and faith.
(Verse 7) Andronicus and Junia were a man and a woman whose ministry was well known, even among the apostles! They took risks for Christ and were imprisoned with Paul.
(Verse 13) Rufus's mother was honored for her love and service. Paul honors her like his own mother. This shows how important mothers are in God’s church!
(Verse 21) Timothy also traveled with Paul as his co-worker. He believed through the faith of his mother and grandmother. Timothy’s church planting ministry was a family legacy!
Ask
What did you learn from these Scriptures?
Think a little, how will you practice what you have learned?
